newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: China threatens to veto Guatemala peacekeepers.
newsitem.headline: China threatens to veto Guatemala peacekeepers.

text.p: China said it would veto a resolution authorising 155 peacekeepers for Guatemala if the issue were pressed to a vote on Friday without concessions from the Central American country over its ties to Taiwan.

China's spokesman Chen Ranfeng told reporters: "We can wait, we are open-minded, we hope that this issue can be solved satisfactorily. But if the council members would like to proceed with the vote then China is ready to vote and we will vote against."

The council is consulting on when to press for a vote on the resolution, sponsored by the United States among others. The measure would allow the U.N. military observers to go to Guatemala for three months as part of a U.N.-brokered peace plan signed on Dec. 29 in Guatemala City.

Beijing has used its veto only twice in the council since it unseated Nationalist China and took its seat in 1971. it blocked the U.N. membership of Bangladesh in August, 1972, and used its veto again the following month in connection with an amendment to a Middle East resolution.

Chinese and Guatemalan envoys have been negotiating for the past month, and Chen said Guatemala had sent China a letter that was not satisfactory. Guatemala has diplomatic relations with Taiwan, which gives it considerable economic aid.

"For the Chinese people, maintaining their national sovereignty and territorial integrity is the most important thing," Chen said, adding that Beijing also was annoyed at the appearance of Taiwan's foreign minister, John Chang, at the Dec. 29 ceremonies in Guatemala City.
